title: Run, Test, and Celebrate!
description: Run your app and see the output.

slides.title: Let’s Run It! 🏃
slides.content:
# Two Ways to Start

1. **In your IDE**: Find the `DemoApplication` class and click the green ▶️ button next to the `main` method.
2. **Terminal**: Navigate to the project folder and run:
   ```bash
   ./mvnw spring-boot:run
   ```

slides.title: Expected Output
slides.content: After a few seconds you’ll see something like:
slides.codeSnippet: Started DemoApplication in 2.5 seconds (JVM running for 3.1)

slides.title: Test Your API 🌐
slides.content:
# Open a browser or use `curl`

Go to: [http://localhost:8080/hello](http://localhost:8080/hello)

You should see:

```
Hello, Spring Boot!
```

Congratulations – you just built your first Spring Boot web application! 🎉

quizData.question: What is the default port that Spring Boot runs on?
quizData.explanation: Spring Boot runs an embedded Tomcat server on port **8080** by default. You can change it in `application.properties`.
